ti: Fix reduceKernel — closure call, odometer and F32 pre-widening on every element
Make broadcastKernel copy contiguous runs instead of walking an odometer per element
Remove the per-element indirect call and bounds checks from the elementwise kernels

note: Implemented and validated. broadcastKernel hoists the innermost axis out of the per-element odometer: each run is a copy (source stride 1) or a fill (stride 0), and the odometer ticks once per run. MEASURED 160,540 -> 35,730 ns on BenchmarkBroadcastF64_256to256x256, 4.49x, via an interleaved three-round A/B with a file-copy toggle on the same host in one session. An earlier non-interleaved comparison suggested 5.5x and was DISCARDED: the untouched BenchmarkReshapeF64_64K control moved 46.4 to 37.0 us between those sessions, proving the runs were not comparable. BIT-IDENTITY: exact equality rather than tolerance, since the op does no arithmetic. TestBroadcastRunsMatchesPerElement pins it element-for-element against the per-element traversal across F32 and F64 for a trailing verbatim row, a trailing broadcast axis, a mixed rank-3 case and a rank-0 output; proven NON-VACUOUS by mutation (moving the odometer tick to the innermost axis turns it red, restoring turns it green). Added BenchmarkBroadcastReplicateF64 and BenchmarkBroadcastMixedF64 for the regimes the pre-existing benchmark never covered. Gates: gofmt and go vet clean, backend/... and autograd green; nn carries two pre-existing bit-identity failures identical on unmodified main (goai#385), unrelated. NOT DONE: the perfscan rule for the scalar-copy-with-contiguous-run pattern remains outstanding and is still required by the standing contract; left to the detector work rather than bundled here. Recorded in docs/benchmarking.md.
